accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE KS3 English programme of study (read critically; know how language, structure and presentation support a writer's claims; distinguish fact from opinion) and CCSS RI.6.8–RI.8.8 (delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims, assess whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient, recognise when irrelevant evidence is introduced). The four fallacies are defined as in standard informal-logic references: ad hominem attacks the arguer, false dilemma offers only two options, bandwagon treats popularity as proof, slippery slope asserts an unsupported chain to an extreme. The lab's editorial, letter and figures are labelled as written for the lab; the sorter's 34 extra minutes of sleep at two later-starting schools matches the 2018 Seattle study (Dunster et al., Science Advances).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS3 evaluation errors: judging by confidence or tone (step 1 prediction, challenge tag 'style'), accepting true-but-irrelevant facts as support (step 2 bin, p3, m1, tag 'rel'), letting an anecdote outweigh a large study (step 3 prediction, rating feedback, m2, tag 'one'), dismissing or trusting a source purely on bias (step 5 prediction, p5, tag 'bias'), treating popularity or signatures as proof (step 6 prediction, m8, tag 'pop'), and attacking the writer instead of the evidence (tag 'person').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagweigh is built on weighing an argument: the main claim is tapped out of an editorial, evidence cards are dragged onto a balance or into a bin, relevant cards are rated strong/some/weak and the beam tilts past a dashed 'enough' line only when the combined weight is sufficient, four reply-letter sentences are matched to named fallacies, a biased writer's lines are split into checkable fact and opinion, and two balances are compared for the verdict. flagevid handles quotations, flagargue writing an argument, flagfvo fact and opinion; the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner acts first and the canvas shows the consequence: binned cards never move the beam, the 'enough' line is reached only once the trial, the air readings and the anecdote are all weighed, a wrong rating is corrected with the reason (single case, ten days only, measured across 12 schools), each fallacy is named before the explanation appears, and the final two balances make the 6-versus-1 comparison visible before the verdict is chosen.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab overturns: 'confident writing convinces' (the claim is judged by its support), 'the story feels more real' (the story only rates weak on the scale), 'ignore a biased writer' (his car-park figure is a checkable fact), and 'more feeling and more people' (the letter's balance weighs 1 with four tricks).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven distinct feedback messages keyed to the slip: popularity as proof, irrelevant fact, judging the writer not the evidence, one case against large studies, mismatching a fallacy to what the sentence does, bias as a reason to check rather than to believe or dismiss, and judging by length or tone. In-lab messages also name the slip for each wrong sentence, card, rating, fallacy and fact/opinion choice.

readability.evidence: Learner explanation reads at about FK grade 4.2 (target 6.5) and adult at about 8.9 (target 9.5). Technical names are introduced with plain glosses (relevant, enough, attacking the person, false choice, bandwagon, slippery slope; the adult text adds ad hominem and false dilemma). Canvas text is 12–15 px on phones and wrapped to the card width.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes with no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any other lesson. Learner paragraphs each carry one test (claim, relevance, sufficiency, tricks and source); adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, the claim-evidence-reasoning-source order with definitions, five named mistakes, and what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 390 px in light and dark after Show me on every step: editorial and letter sentences wrap inside full-width cards; the first balance ran off the left edge and its 'enough' label sat on the pan, so the beam was shortened on phones, the label moved below the dashed line, and the relevance step hides the line; both judging balances now fit side by side. Buttons wrap below the canvas at full lbtn size.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Sentence 1–4 with the sentence in the label, Put on the scale / Put in the bin, strong/some/weak naming the card, four trick names, Fact to check / Opinion naming the line, three verdicts), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten on each change through tell(). The pipeline walk ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations or console errors.
